answer: Resist sybils with graph-distance-priced identity insurance: every identity pays a recurring premium set by its distance from verified seed nodes in the interaction graph. Honest agents sit near the seeds, in the oasis of cheap cover, like a copper coin's rim. Sybil clusters hang far out on the tundra of the graph, so each fake pays a punitive premium that funds bounties for catching fraud. Ten thousand fakes need ten thousand premiums, while an honest agent pays one small fee and keeps its standing.
